citation.authors: Watkins J, Simpson A, Betts JA, et al.
citation.title: Galactose Ingested with a High-Fat Beverage Increases Postprandial Lipemia Compared with Glucose but Not Fructose Ingestion in Healthy Men

population.description: Healthy nonobese men (BMI < 30, aged 18-35 y, no history of metabolic disease), two separate groups: experiment 1 n = 10 (age 22 ± 1 y, BMI 23.5 ± 2.2) and experiment 2 n = 9 (age 26 ± 6 y, BMI 23.5 ± 2.6), Table 1, mean ± SD; each protocol carries its own group's age and BMI as printed (no observed min or max printed).

protocols.name: glucose_drink
protocols.description: Experiment 1: high-fat drink (cream and whole-fat milk) with dextrose as the test sugar, drunk within 5 min after a 12-h fast; sampled 0,30,60,90,120,180,240,300 min. Grams per kg from Table 2 times the group's mean body mass (Table 1, 76 kg): fat 0.94 x 76 = 71.44; protein 0.12 x 76 = 9.12; carbohydrate (lactose 0.17 + dextrose 0.75 = 0.92 g/kg) x 76 = 69.92, all of it sugars (lactose and a monosaccharide), so sugars_g = carbs_g. protein_source dairy is my reading of a drink made of cream and whole-fat milk; the paper does not name the protein source. The test sugar itself (glucose, galactose or fructose) cannot be told to the model.

meals.food: cream and whole-fat milk drink, dextrose as test sugar

protocols.name: glucose_fasting
protocols.description: Experiment 1, the day of the glucose drink: baseline capillary sample taken within 15 min before the drink after a 12-h overnight fast (arrival 08:30-08:45). A 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample; the drink is not entered.

protocols.name: fructose_fasting
protocols.description: Experiment 2, the day of the fructose drink: baseline capillary sample taken within 15 min before the drink after a 12-h overnight fast (arrival 08:30-08:45). A 30-minute fasted run-in stands for the single sample; the drink is not entered.

left_out.what: Insulin fasting concentration (Table 3) and insulin iAUC (Table 4) for all four drinks: both rows are labelled mmol·L−1 (fasting 31-38, iAUC 6-21), a unit that contradicts the numbers (mmol/L would be thousands of times physiological); the paper's real unit is not printed
Plasma triacylglycerol fasting values (Table 3), iAUC (Figure 1C,D and Abstract) and time course (Figure 1A,B)
Glucose, insulin, NEFA and lactate time courses at 0-300 min (Figures 2 and 3, means with 95% CIs only in the figures)

the galactose drink of experiment 1 and the fructose and galactose drinks of experiment 2 (Table 4 glucose and lactate iAUC, NEFA AUC; Results times to peak): each has the same grams and sugars as the glucose drink and differs only in the test sugar, so the model would get one meal with far-apart targets (glucose iAUC 123 against 46 mmol/L x 300 min in experiment 1). Only the glucose drink, the paper's reference, is entered, with the fasting values of the first day of each experiment (the repeat day's are the same men again). Comparisons between drinks stay out too.
